notes: EBIT in the historical section is GAAP operating income from CRL’s consolidated financial statements; FY2025 GAAP operating income is extremely low due to large non-cash charges (impairments), so the base-case EBIT margin path uses normalized profitability assumptions rather than extrapolating GAAP directly. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1100682/000110068226000022/crl-20251227.htm))

NWC construction is simplified as: (Total current assets - Cash and cash equivalents) - Total current liabilities. This excludes cash but does not separately adjust for any other short-term investments or potential classification nuances; see lines in the balance sheets for the underlying totals. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1100682/000110068226000022/crl-20251227.htm))

Tax rate assumption is set to the statutory U.S. rate (0.21) because FY2025 effective tax rate is negative due to impairment effects; cash taxes and normalized tax capacity are not explicitly disclosed in a directly usable form for forecasting in the retrieved excerpts. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1100682/000110068226000022/crl-20251227.htm))

WACC (0.085) and terminal exit EBITDA multiple (16.0) are modeling assumptions without a specific management-provided WACC or terminal multiple in the retrieved sources; replace with your required market-implied inputs if your pipeline requires strict provenance.

NOL balance is represented by the tax-effected deferred tax asset for net operating loss carryforwards disclosed in the FY2025 10-K ($332.5 million). NOL utilization percent (0.80) is assumed and not explicitly provided in the retrieved sources. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1100682/000110068226000022/crl-20251227.htm))

Comps market-multiple fields (EV/NTM Revenue, EV/NTM EBITDA, P/NTM) are left null due to missing retrieval of a consistent market-multiples dataset in this run; populate from your preferred market-data provider to complete the comp section.

catalysts: DSA bookings converting into reported revenue (particularly 2H 2026 per guidance). ([biospace.com](https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/charles-river-laboratories-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results-and-provides-2026-guidance))

Further realization of restructuring/efficiency savings supporting sustained margin recovery. ([biospace.com](https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/charles-river-laboratories-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results-and-provides-2026-guidance))

Manufacturing profitability stabilization as demand and customer dynamics normalize after prior headwinds. ([biospace.com](https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/charles-river-laboratories-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results-and-provides-2026-guidance))
company_overview: Global provider of preclinical drug development services and research models, organized into three segments: RMS, DSA, and Manufacturing Solutions. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1100682/000110068226000022/crl-20251227.htm))

FY2025 revenue was $4.015 billion; DSA was the largest segment at approximately 59.8% of total revenue. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1100682/000110068226000022/crl-20251227.htm))

At FY2025 year-end (Dec 27, 2025), cash and cash equivalents were $213.8 million, and total debt and finance leases were $2.152 billion. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1100682/000110068226000022/crl-20251227.htm))
current_context: FY2025 revenue declined 0.9% to $4.02 billion; GAAP operating margin fell to 0.6% (non-GAAP operating margin cited as 19.8%). ([biospace.com](https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/charles-river-laboratories-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results-and-provides-2026-guidance))

2026 guidance calls for reported revenue growth at least flat to +1.5% and non-GAAP EPS of $10.70 to $11.20, assuming DSA bookings stabilization and continued efficiency initiatives. ([biospace.com](https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/charles-river-laboratories-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results-and-provides-2026-guidance))

Management expects return to organic revenue growth in the second half of 2026, with Manufacturing and RMS impacts partially offsetting the DSA recovery. ([biospace.com](https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/charles-river-laboratories-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results-and-provides-2026-guidance))
investment_highlights: Base case assumes modest top-line recovery beginning in 2026, consistent with management’s ‘at least flat to +1.5%’ reported revenue guidance. ([biospace.com](https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/charles-river-laboratories-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results-and-provides-2026-guidance))

Margin trajectory in the base case reflects normalization toward a mid-to-high teens operating margin as impairments are non-recurring and efficiency actions continue. ([biospace.com](https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/charles-river-laboratories-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results-and-provides-2026-guidance))

Capex intensity is modeled slightly above the trough in FY2025, consistent with recent capex as a share of sales (historically ~5–8%). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1100682/000110068226000022/crl-20251227.htm))

Working capital intensity is assumed to gradually normalize from FY2025’s unusually low level (structural drivers not fully disclosed; see notes). ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1100682/000110068226000022/crl-20251227.htm))
key_risks: GAAP earnings volatility from large non-cash charges (e.g., impairments) may delay margin normalization vs. the base-case EBIT path. ([biospace.com](https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/charles-river-laboratories-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results-and-provides-2026-guidance))

Biopharma demand environment could remain softer than assumed, limiting revenue growth and operating leverage. ([biospace.com](https://www.biospace.com/press-releases/charles-river-laboratories-announces-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-2025-results-and-provides-2026-guidance))

Working capital may not normalize as expected if billing/deferred revenue dynamics differ from the simplified NWC construction used here. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1100682/000110068226000022/crl-20251227.htm))

valuation_summary: DCF base case uses internally chained revenue growth from the FY2025 revenue base and applies a gradual EBIT margin mean reversion to reflect normalized profitability. ([sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1100682/000110068226000022/crl-20251227.htm))
Terminal value uses an exit-multiple framework with conservative long-run growth assumptions; bull/bear scenarios capture multiple and discount-rate uncertainty.
Comps set includes CRO and adjacent preclinical/clinical service providers, but market-multiple inputs are left null pending external data (see notes).
